evals.name: tokyo-family-trip-with-partial-coverage-and-shopping
evals.prompt: Build an .xlsx travel itinerary workbook from a hotel PDF, outbound e-ticket PDF, attraction screenshots, conference dates, and shopping notes for a four-person Tokyo trip.
evals.expected_output: The response uses this skill, extracts facts first, consolidates known blockers and follows up only for materially new safety or correctness issues, then produces an .xlsx workbook with the required sheet order, coverage flags, protected conference days, and shopping still visible.

assertions.text: Skill triggers for workbook generation
Known blockers are consolidated without repeated questions; material new safety or correctness issues may receive focused follow-up
Workbook is created
Coverage review flags remain visible
Shopping remains visible in Daily Plan and Buy List

evals.name: multi-city-leisure-trip-with-solid-bookings
evals.prompt: Turn these Paris-Lyon-Nice bookings and short notes into a trip spreadsheet. The bookings are complete, but the daily plan should stay geographically sensible.
evals.expected_output: The skill uses the same workbook architecture, names the options sheet appropriately for a non-Tokyo trip, preserves booked anchors, and avoids absurd cross-city daily routes.

assertions.text: Options sheet name adapts for non-Tokyo travel
Daily plans stay geographically coherent
No Tokyo-only labels leak into the workbook

evals.name: solo-work-trip-with-fixed-conference
evals.prompt: Create an xlsx conference travel workbook for a solo Berlin work trip with fixed event days and no shopping goals.
evals.expected_output: The workbook protects the conference days, keeps shopping minimal rather than invented, and still includes the workbook tabs for prep, pack, buy, and sources.

assertions.text: Conference days are protected in Daily Plan
Shopping is not hallucinated when absent
Workbook still includes the full sheet order

evals.name: traveller-count-mismatch-needs-consolidated-clarification
evals.prompt: Build a holiday itinerary spreadsheet from conflicting hotel and flight documents where the hotel covers 3 adults and the flights show 2, but the notes talk about 4 travellers.
evals.expected_output: The skill consolidates known coverage questions, follows up if new critical evidence appears, and keeps unresolved mismatches visible as review flags rather than silently choosing one source.

assertions.text: Known contradictions are addressed together without a hard cap that prevents necessary follow-up
Contradictions become review flags
The skill does not silently overwrite one source with another

evals.name: negative-markdown-itinerary-request
evals.prompt: Write me a markdown itinerary for Kyoto with a few things to do each day. I do not need a spreadsheet.
evals.expected_output: This skill should not be the primary tool because the user asked for prose, not workbook generation.

assertions.text: Skill should not be the primary tool

evals.name: rough-notes-only-no-uploaded-files
evals.prompt: I only have rough notes for a family Singapore trip. Build a travel prep spreadsheet and itinerary workbook anyway, using assumptions and visible flags where needed.
evals.expected_output: The skill generates a workbook from rough notes, consolidates known blockers with focused follow-up for materially new safety or correctness issues, and uses assumptions and review flags for non-blockers instead of freezing.

assertions.text: Workbook can be generated without uploaded files
Assumptions are explicit
The skill does not stall on non-blockers

evals.name: no-return-flight-yet
evals.prompt: Make a trip spreadsheet for a Lisbon trip where the outbound flight and hotel are booked but the return flight is not booked yet.
evals.expected_output: The skill still generates the workbook, keeps the missing return coverage visible in review flags and prep actions, and does not hallucinate a return booking.

assertions.text: Workbook still gets created
Missing return coverage is flagged clearly
No fake return booking is invented

evals.name: new-transit-blocker-after-intake
evals.prompt: We already answered the intake: two travellers, Tokyo trip from 2027-04-05 to 2027-04-12, both returning home on April 13, no mobility constraints. A newly supplied flight document reveals an overnight transfer requiring entry into another country, but only one traveller's passport nationality is known. Continue the workbook; don't re-ask the dates or group size.
evals.expected_output: Asks a focused follow-up about the newly material passport/transit facts rather than guessing because an earlier intake occurred. Reuses settled dates and group size, verifies relevant official entry rules, and flags unresolved compliance.

assertions.text: Follows up on the newly material transit or nationality uncertainty without reinterviewing answered context
Does not guess entry eligibility or claim current rules were verified without official evidence
Uses only useful intake groupings and keeps unresolved coverage or compliance visible

evals.name: unsupported-workbook-layout-is-not-a-fake-flag
evals.prompt: Use this travel workbook skill, but I need a single-sheet dashboard with a custom palette and no other tabs. Discover spreadsheet guidance through this harness; do not assume a vendor installation path. Do not change the builder source without asking.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the bundled builder and validator enforce a different workbook contract, then proposes an alternative workflow or scoped extension rather than inventing customization flags or claiming the normal validator supports the requested shape.

assertions.text: Discovers available guidance through the harness rather than a fixed home-directory path
Distinguishes supported builder output from a proposed alternative or extension
Does not silently edit the canonical or installed builder or claim unsupported flags or validation coverage
